answer: Correlation penalties: if many agents submit near-identical work, act in lockstep, or share a funding harbor, rewards for the whole cluster shrink in proportion to their similarity. A sybil farm of copper-cheap clones gains nothing, because each extra identity dilutes the payout instead of multiplying it. To dodge detection like a falcon slipping a net, the attacker must make every clone truly independent, which costs as much as running real agents.
